description:
The server's graceful-shutdown tests observe the drain and the force-close through explicit signals instead of timed log scraping, so they pass deterministically alone and under parallel load.

## Background

`test_the_drain_assertion_rejects_a_server_that_force_closes_early` in `crates/server/tests/server_integration/graceful_shutdown_tests.rs` failed in an authoritative branch CI run (2026-11-04) with "no log line reports \"force-closing\"" at line 256, and passed five times in a row when run alone on the same commit. The suite observes server behaviour by polling the process log with sleeps (`READ_POLL`), with a one-second configured drain deadline (`CONFIGURED_DRAIN_DEADLINE`) and a one-second observation window (`STOPPED_OBSERVATION_WINDOW`), and reads the drain duration back out of log fields. Under parallel load the log line can arrive after the observation ends. The project's test rules require deterministic tests that never wait on wall-clock time to observe the property they own.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every stalled-connection fixture in `graceful_shutdown_tests.rs` returns only after the server has begun reading that connection: preferably by sending a partial request (a request line without its terminating blank line) and waiting on an existing server-side signal of the read, or, only if no existing signal proves the read, on an explicit first-read event the server emits under `test-support`. The fixture never polls or waits on wall-clock time to establish that state.
- [hard] REQ-02: Any hook added for REQ-01 compiles only under `test-support`, adds no production code path or dependency, and is enabled only through an environment variable set on the test child process; production behaviour and log lines are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each graceful-shutdown test keeps the property it owns, with no weakened assertion and no ignored or deleted test.
- [hard] REQ-04: The suite passes 20 consecutive runs alone and 20 runs inside a full parallel workspace test run.

## Decisions

- D-01: The original criteria attributed the flake to timed log scraping and required an explicit shutdown event in its place. Investigation showed the log is read only after the process exits, so it is complete; the race is that a "stalled" connection can still be in hyper-util's version-detection state when shutdown starts, so graceful shutdown cancels it and nothing is force-closed. The criteria were rewritten to establish the state the property needs (steward ruling, 2026-11-04). Original REQ-01: "observes the force-close through an explicit signal or event the server emits ... not by polling log text against a time window." Original REQ-02 extended that to every sibling test.

## Notes

The production shutdown behaviour and its log lines stay unchanged; only how tests observe them changes, plus whatever minimal seam the server needs to emit the signal.
title: Graceful-shutdown tests observe the server through explicit signals
